# Bank Feeds API routes

Open-banking connection management. Supports the two implemented providers (`extension`, `manual_csv`) for linking bank accounts to IsaFlow, triggering syncs, and inspecting sync history. Delegates to `services/bank/openBankingService.ts`.

## Endpoints

| Method + path | Handler | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/accounting/bank-feeds` | `index.ts` | List all active connections for the company. Response: `{ items, count }`. |
| `POST /api/accounting/bank-feeds` | `index.ts` | Create a new connection. Body: `{ provider, accountId?, externalAccountId?, config? }`. |
| `DELETE /api/accounting/bank-feeds/[id]` | `[id].ts` | Soft-delete a connection. |
| `POST /api/accounting/bank-feeds/[id]/sync` | `[id]/sync.ts` | Trigger a manual sync for a connection. Returns sync result. |
| `GET /api/accounting/bank-feeds/[id]/logs` | `[id]/logs.ts` | Fetch sync history. Optional `?limit` (max 50, default 10). Response: `{ items, count }`. |

## Auth

- `index.ts` and `[id].ts`: `withAuth(withErrorHandler(withCsrf(handler)))` — CSRF enforced on all methods (including GET on index — the CSRF wrapper allows GETs through but logs are consistent).
- `[id]/sync.ts`: `withAuth(withErrorHandler(withCsrf(handler)))` — CSRF enforced.
- `[id]/logs.ts`: `withAuth(withErrorHandler(handler))` — no CSRF (read-only).

## Response contract

All routes use `apiResponse.success` / `.badRequest` / `.notFound`. Creation returns HTTP 201 via `apiResponse.success(res, connection, 'Connection created', 201)`. Clients MUST unwrap `json.data`.

## Business rules / gotchas

- Valid providers: `extension | manual_csv`. Any other provider (including the never-implemented `basiq | tink | plaid`) → 400. Syncing a legacy `basiq`/`tink`/`plaid` connection fails with "provider is not implemented" instead of importing fabricated rows (K-018).
- `config` is a free-form JSON object; structure depends on provider.
- DELETE is a soft-delete — the service sets an inactive flag; it does not hard-delete.
- Sync logs are capped server-side at 50 per call regardless of `?limit`.
